text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The prosecutor's office started a case against troubled Tauras Bank. It is suspected that nine million ECU out of a 17 million ECU European Union credit granted to the country via Tauras Bank in 1995 was squandered.
- The government decided to raise salaries to doctors by 18.2 percent from July 1.
- Preliminary statistics department data said that the country's trade deficit in the first four months of the year was 2.338 billion litas.
- The stock exchange decided to suspend the trade with the shares of Lithuanian Energy from June 30 to September 1 due to the reorganisation of the company.

- Statistics department preliminary data said that 9.5 litres of pure alcohol per capita were consumed in Lithuania but experts think it was higher since the official statistics do not include the consumption of illegally imported alcohol.
- Lithuanian and Polish defence ministers signed an agreement to found a joint peace keeping batallion Litpolbat.
- The government approved the reoprganisation plan of Lithuanian Energy by separating the heating branch of the firm and passing it to municipal control.
- Tauras bank might be declared insolvent on Thursday.
- Heating energy prices might rise around 20 percent from the beginning of July and possibly more.
- The real average salary in Lithuania has increased by 4.4 percent in May compared to April, the statistics department said.
- The crime rate in Lithuania in the first five months of the year increased by 15.4 percent compared to the same period in 1996.
